feedback.problem:
A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=12\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t),$ where $t\ge 0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=3\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s},$ calculate the maximum velocity ${v}_{\text{max}}$ of the particle and determine the earliest time when the particle reaches its maximum velocity.

feedback.worked_solution:
The extrema of the velocity $v$ occur at the critical points of $v.$  

Since $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=a(t),$ to find the times where $v$ is a maximum, we just need to solve $a(t)=0$ and test each solution using the first or second derivative test.

Solving $a(t)=0$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =0 \\ 12\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t) & =0 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(4t) & =0 \\ 4t & =\frac{\pi }{2}+\pi n \\ t & =\frac{\pi }{8}+\frac{\pi }{4}n,\end{aligned}
$$

where $n$ is any integer.  

Therefore, the extrema of the velocity function, for $t>0,$ are

$$
t=\frac{\pi }{8},\frac{3\pi }{8},\frac{5\pi }{8},…
$$

We now test the extrema values, starting with the least, using the second derivative test. For this, we find the second derivative of $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}v}{\text{d}{t}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(a(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(12\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)) \\  & =-48\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t).\end{aligned}
$$

At $t=\frac{\pi }{8},$ the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{8}) & =-48\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\cdot \frac{\pi }{8}) \\  & =-48\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =-48\cdot 1 \\  & =-48<0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${v}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{8})<0,$ we conclude that the velocity is maximized when $t=\frac{\pi }{8}.$  Therefore, the first time when the particle reaches its maximum velocity is $t=\frac{\pi }{8}\,\text{s}.$

Now, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int 12\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)\text{d}t \\  & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=3.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+C & =3 \\ 0+C & =3\,⟹\,C=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is

$$
v(t)=3+3\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t).
$$

Finally, we calculate the maximum velocity:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{\text{max}} & =v(\frac{\pi }{8}) \\  & =3+3\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\cdot \frac{\pi }{8}) \\  & =3+3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =6\,\text{m}/\text{s}.\end{aligned}
$$

So the maximum velocity  ${v}_{\text{max}}=6\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ is reached first time at $t=\frac{\pi }{8}\,\text{s}.$
